They appear here as they start
Stop and turn off the hotspot
Turning the hotspot off now cuts them off mid-install. They will be left unfinished and will need setting up again from the start.
Wait until the status says nothing is part-way through, and stopping is safe.
Everything installed and the lock is on.
Set the hotspot up by hand
If this phone cannot start a hotspot on its own, turn on the hotspot in Settings, then type its name and password here.
To start its own hotspot this phone needs the nearby Wi-Fi permission. Allow it in Settings, or set the hotspot up by hand below.
This deployment does not fit in a code a phone camera can read reliably. Remove some apps, or shorten the deployment name.
Allow this by hand on the device: %1$s
1. Start a deployment on this phone. A square code appears.
2. Factory reset the new phone, or take it out of the box.
3. On its first “Hello” screen, tap the middle of the screen six times.
4. The phone opens a camera. Point it at the square code.
5. The phone joins this phone\'s hotspot and installs everything. Leave the two phones near each other.
6. When it finishes, the phone shows the Simple Phone home screen and appears in the list here.
Before you start, disconnect this phone from any Wi-Fi network. If it stays joined to one, the code can send the new phones to the wrong address and they will wait forever.
Bring a power bank. Running the hotspot and sending the apps drains this phone quickly — that, rather than speed, is what limits how many phones you can do in one go.
The phone keeps its own lock screen, so a PIN or pattern can be set on it. Also protects the phone between switching on and the launcher taking over.
No lock screen. The phone wakes straight into the launcher, with nothing to swipe or read.
